WebSearch was already exhausted (0/200 remaining) before I reached this row, and most search engines (Bing, DuckDuckGo HTML/Lite, Startpage, Marginalia) either CAPTCHA'd, bot-blocked, or returned garbage/irrelevant results to both the WebFetch tool and direct curl. Google News RSS (news.google.com/rss/search) was the one search surface that stayed usable. Via that + Wikipedia's own API I found: (1) Wikipedia 'Nandipur Power Project' (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nandipur_Power_Project) -- an independent, detailed, well-cited encyclopedia article confirming a real 425/525MW combined-cycle plant at Nandipur near Gujranwala, Punjab, built by China Dongfang Electric, commissioned 2014, and explicitly: 'On 23 April 2017, Nandipur started a 525 MW test run on regasified liquefied natural gas (RLNG) with 30 million cubic feet ... per day of gas supply from Sui Northern Gas Pipelines limited (SNGPL)', and later 'in April 2018, [SNGPL] disconnected gas supply to the plant for defaulting on dues of approximately Rs. 900 million.' Ownership of the PLANT itself is Government of Punjab / Nandipur Thermal Power Generation Company Limited (NPGCL) -- distinct from the pipeline, which SNGPL (the gas utility) would own, consistent with the sheet's Owner1=SNGPL 100%. (2) Dawn.com, 23 Apr 2017 (dawn.com/news/1328722), reporting the RLNG test-run launch, directly quotes SNGPL's own MD: 'He said the SNGPL had laid a new and dedicated pipeline for provision of RLNG to Nandipur plant' and 'we are providing 10 to 30MMCFD of RLNG to it according to demand.' This is a strong, independent, primary confirmation that a dedicated SNGPL pipeline to Nandipur physically exists and was newly built/operating as of April 2017 -- squarely matching this GEM row (a dedicated feeder from the SNGPL trunk network to the Nandipur plant). (3) Dawn.com, 5 Apr 2018 (dawn.com/news/1379922), a separate, later reporting event, confirms the same relationship still operating a year on: 'The 425MW Nandipur power plant remained shut for four hours ... after ... SNGPL disconnected gas supply to it for defaulting on dues of around Rs900 million' (matches Wikipedia's Rs900m figure independently). (4) Wikipedia 'List of power stations in Pakistan' lists 'TPS Nandipur' (Gujranwala, Punjab, gas-fired) sourced to NEPRA's 'State of Industry Report 2024', and Google News turns up a Business Recorder/Dawn/Tribune cluster from Dec 2025-Jul 2026 discussing privatisation of 'Guddu and Nandipur power plants' -- i.e. the plant (and by necessity its gas feed) is still a live, operating asset as of this pass's date (2026-08-07), not decommissioned or phantom. Taken together this is 2+ genuinely independent origins (Dawn primary reporting with a direct SNGPL-MD quote, and Wikipedia's separately-sourced overview, cross-checked against a second Dawn report a year later) confirming the underlying entity is real, gas-fired, and specifically fed by a dedicated SNGPL pipeline -- this is NOT a GEM-only/hallucinated row. CLASSIFICATION: PipelineType=transmission and Fuel=Gas are both consistent with this being a dedicated, high-pressure trunk feeder (Dawn's own description: 'new and dedicated pipeline') rather than a gathering/lateral line; the same transmission classification is used throughout this roster for comparable single-consumer feeder lines (e.g. P4102 AV22-Kot Addu, P4103 D.G. Khan, P4104 Dhodak-Kot Addu, all also feeding specific plants/consumers), so no classification concern. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 63-pipeline roster. This is NOT a duplicate/double-count; it is two distinct, adjoining physical segments. P4137 'Sheikhupura-Gujranwala Gas Pipeline' (59.44 km, 10in) is a different, smaller-diameter line between the same two general areas -- plausible as a parallel/older line rather than the same pipe as this 24in dedicated RLNG feeder, and I found no basis to call it a duplicate either (different diameter, different length, and P4138's own name explicitly frames it as a power-plant-specific dedicated line, distinct in character from a general district transmission pipeline).
